phases.name: Plan
phases.summary: Is it worth doing, and what exactly?

phases.name: Deliver
phases.summary: Build it, prove it, release it

stages.name: Discover
stages.purpose: Frame the opportunity. Confirm the problem is real, valuable, and that AI is plausibly the right tool.
stages.keyQuestion: Is this a problem worth solving with AI?

stages.name: Assess
stages.purpose: Evaluate feasibility, data, risk, and value before committing to a design.
stages.keyQuestion: Can we do this responsibly, and is it worth it?

stages.name: Design
stages.tagline: Define it and how to judge it
stages.purpose: Define the solution, how it will be evaluated, how humans stay in control, and how success is measured.
stages.keyQuestion: What exactly are we building, and how will we know it works?

stages.name: Build
stages.purpose: Build a working solution with versioned configuration, a test plan, and documented limitations.
stages.keyQuestion: Does a working, traceable version exist?

stages.name: Validate
stages.purpose: Prove the solution performs, is safe enough to operate, and is accepted by the business.
stages.keyQuestion: Is the evidence strong enough to put this in front of real users?

stages.name: Deploy
stages.purpose: Release to production with support, training, rollback, and monitoring in place.
stages.keyQuestion: Are people, process, and monitoring ready for go-live?

stages.name: Operate
stages.purpose: Run the solution, watch for drift and incidents, and measure adoption and realized value.
stages.keyQuestion: Is it working, being used, and delivering value?

stages.name: Improve / Retire
stages.purpose: Continuously improve the solution, re-assess risk after changes, or retire it responsibly.
stages.keyQuestion: Should we invest further, change course, or retire?

riskTiers.name: Low
riskTiers.description: Internal productivity assistance with a human always in the loop, non-sensitive data, and limited blast radius if the AI is wrong.

riskTiers.name: Moderate
riskTiers.summary: Business-critical workflow or material business impact.
riskTiers.description: Supports a business-critical workflow, touches customer data, or influences outcomes with material business impact. A human remains accountable for the final action.
riskTiers.rigor: Adds human oversight validation, security and privacy reviews, monitoring plan, and rollback planning.

riskTiers.name: High
riskTiers.summary: Consequential decisions, sensitive data, high autonomy, or significant exposure.
riskTiers.description: Makes or heavily shapes consequential decisions, acts with autonomy, uses sensitive or regulated data, or carries safety, regulatory, or significant reputational exposure.
riskTiers.rigor: Adds autonomy boundaries, implemented override controls, adversarial and bias testing, executive residual-risk acceptance, and governance board deployment approval.

readinessDimensions.name: Business Value
readinessDimensions.description: Is the outcome defined, the value hypothesis credible, and value being measured?

readinessDimensions.name: Product Readiness
readinessDimensions.description: Is the problem, user experience, scope, and limitation story clear and agreed?

readinessDimensions.name: Technical Readiness
readinessDimensions.description: Is the solution feasible, built, integrated, versioned, and backed by suitable data?

readinessDimensions.name: AI Evaluation
readinessDimensions.description: Has the AI been evaluated against defined criteria, at the right scale, with results documented?

readinessDimensions.name: Risk & Governance
readinessDimensions.description: Are risks assessed, mitigated, reviewed, and residual risk explicitly accepted?

readinessDimensions.name: Operational Readiness
readinessDimensions.description: Are support, monitoring, incident management, and rollback ready?

readinessDimensions.name: Adoption Readiness
readinessDimensions.description: Are users identified, trained, bought in, and is adoption being measured?

roles.name: Executive Sponsor
roles.responsibilities: Owns the business case, removes obstacles, and accepts residual risk.

roles.name: Product Manager
roles.responsibilities: Orchestrates the lifecycle, owns scope, priorities, and gate readiness.

roles.name: Business Owner
roles.responsibilities: Owns the target workflow and accepts the solution through UAT.

roles.name: AI / Solution Architect
roles.responsibilities: Owns the solution design, model and pattern choices, and known limitations.

roles.name: Engineering
roles.responsibilities: Builds, integrates, versions, and hardens the solution.

roles.name: Data Owner
roles.responsibilities: Validates data quality, rights to use, and lineage of knowledge sources.

roles.name: UX / Research
roles.responsibilities: Researches users and designs the workflow, including review and override moments.

roles.name: Security
roles.responsibilities: Assesses security threats, prompt-injection exposure, and access controls.

roles.name: Privacy / Legal
roles.responsibilities: Reviews personal data use, consent, and legal obligations.

roles.name: QA / Evaluation
roles.responsibilities: Defines evaluation criteria, runs test suites, and reports results.

roles.name: Operations
roles.responsibilities: Prepares support, monitoring, incident response, and runbooks.

roles.name: Governance / Risk
roles.responsibilities: Runs risk reviews and ensures governance requirements are evidenced.

roles.name: Finance
roles.responsibilities: Validates the value hypothesis and measures realized value.

roles.name: Other / Unknown
roles.responsibilities: Stakeholder with an unclear but persistent interest.

activityTemplates.name: Define the problem statement
activityTemplates.description: Write a crisp problem statement grounded in today's workflow and pain points.
activityTemplates.why: Every later decision is judged against the problem. A vague problem produces a vague solution.
activityTemplates.consequence: Without it, the Discover gate cannot pass and design debates become opinion-driven.

activityTemplates.name: Identify target users and workflow
activityTemplates.description: Name the users, the moment in their workflow the AI supports, and what they do today.
activityTemplates.why: Adoption depends on fitting a real workflow, not a demo.
activityTemplates.consequence: Risk of building for an imagined user.

activityTemplates.name: Define the desired business outcome
activityTemplates.description: State the measurable outcome the business wants, not the feature.
activityTemplates.why: Outcomes anchor value measurement and prioritization.
activityTemplates.consequence: Value cannot be measured or defended later.

activityTemplates.name: Secure an executive sponsor
activityTemplates.description: Confirm an accountable executive who owns the business case.
activityTemplates.why: AI initiatives stall without someone empowered to make trade-offs and accept risk.
activityTemplates.consequence: No one can accept residual risk or approve go-live.

activityTemplates.name: Articulate why AI
activityTemplates.description: Explain why AI beats rules, process change, or existing tools for this problem.
activityTemplates.why: Prevents using AI where simpler, cheaper, more reliable options exist.
activityTemplates.consequence: Risk of unnecessary complexity and cost.

activityTemplates.name: Capture current-state baseline
activityTemplates.description: Measure how the workflow performs today so improvement can be proven.
activityTemplates.why: Without a baseline, realized value is a guess.
activityTemplates.consequence: Value claims will be challenged by Finance.

activityTemplates.name: Complete initial risk assessment
activityTemplates.description: Classify inherent risk, record initial risks, and confirm the risk tier.
activityTemplates.why: The risk tier determines how much rigor the rest of the lifecycle requires.
activityTemplates.consequence: Controls may be under- or over-applied.

activityTemplates.name: Complete data assessment
activityTemplates.description: Assess data availability, quality, access rights, and sensitivity.
activityTemplates.why: AI quality is bounded by data quality, and data rights are a hard constraint.
activityTemplates.consequence: Late discovery of unusable or restricted data.

activityTemplates.name: Assess technical feasibility
activityTemplates.description: Run a spike or prototype to confirm the approach can plausibly meet the bar.
activityTemplates.why: Cheap feasibility checks avoid expensive dead ends.
activityTemplates.consequence: Build may start on an approach that cannot work.

activityTemplates.name: Identify key stakeholders
activityTemplates.description: Assign the business owner, data owner, security, and evaluation leads.
activityTemplates.why: Specialized work needs named owners before it can be scheduled.
activityTemplates.consequence: Activities stall without accountable owners.

activityTemplates.name: Document initial value hypothesis
activityTemplates.description: Quantify expected value and the assumptions behind it.
activityTemplates.why: Investment decisions need a credible, testable value case.
activityTemplates.consequence: The initiative may be deprioritized at the next funding review.

activityTemplates.name: Privacy and legal screening
activityTemplates.description: Screen for personal data, consent, and legal obligations early.
activityTemplates.why: Privacy constraints can change the design fundamentally.
activityTemplates.consequence: Rework or legal exposure discovered late.

activityTemplates.name: Define autonomy level and decision boundaries
activityTemplates.description: Decide what the AI may do on its own and what always requires a human.
activityTemplates.why: Autonomy is the largest driver of consequence when the AI is wrong.
activityTemplates.consequence: Unbounded autonomy cannot pass governance review.

activityTemplates.name: Evaluate build vs. buy options
activityTemplates.description: Compare vendor, platform, and custom options.
activityTemplates.why: Avoids rebuilding commodity capability.
activityTemplates.consequence: Possible overspend.

activityTemplates.name: Produce solution design
activityTemplates.description: Document architecture, model/pattern choice, integrations, and data flow.
activityTemplates.why: A shared design lets security, data, and engineering review the same thing.
activityTemplates.consequence: Build starts without agreement and reviews happen too late.

activityTemplates.name: Define evaluation approach
activityTemplates.description: Set evaluation criteria, datasets, thresholds, and the acceptance bar.
activityTemplates.why: If you can't define good, you can't prove the AI is good enough.
activityTemplates.consequence: Validation becomes subjective and gate reviews stall.

activityTemplates.name: Design human oversight approach
activityTemplates.description: Define where humans review, approve, correct, or override AI output.
activityTemplates.why: Human oversight is the primary control for AI error in business workflows.
activityTemplates.consequence: The solution cannot demonstrate accountable human control.

activityTemplates.name: Document security and privacy considerations
activityTemplates.description: Threat model the solution and decide on data handling controls.
activityTemplates.why: Security and privacy are far cheaper to design in than bolt on.
activityTemplates.consequence: Late security findings force redesign.

activityTemplates.name: Define success metrics and targets
activityTemplates.description: Define business, adoption, and AI performance metrics with baselines and targets.
activityTemplates.why: Metrics turn the value hypothesis into something you can manage.
activityTemplates.consequence: No way to prove the solution delivered value.

activityTemplates.name: Design user experience and workflow integration
activityTemplates.description: Prototype how the AI shows up in the user's workflow and test it with users.
activityTemplates.why: Good AI with a poor workflow fit does not get used.
activityTemplates.consequence: Adoption risk.

activityTemplates.name: Plan expanded evaluation (adversarial and bias)
activityTemplates.description: Plan red-team, bias, and misuse testing proportionate to the risk.
activityTemplates.why: High-risk AI must be tested for how it fails, not just how it succeeds.
activityTemplates.consequence: High-risk deployment cannot be justified.

activityTemplates.name: Draft change management approach
activityTemplates.description: Outline stakeholder impacts, communications, and training needs.
activityTemplates.why: Adoption is designed, not hoped for.
activityTemplates.consequence: Late scramble on training and comms.

activityTemplates.name: Build working solution
activityTemplates.description: Deliver an end-to-end working solution in a non-production environment.
activityTemplates.why: Validation needs something real to validate.
activityTemplates.consequence: Nothing to evaluate.

activityTemplates.name: Record configuration and version information
activityTemplates.description: Version the model, prompts, retrieval settings, and parameters.
activityTemplates.why: You cannot validate, monitor, or roll back what you cannot identify.
activityTemplates.consequence: Evaluation results can't be tied to a specific version.

activityTemplates.name: Prepare test plan
activityTemplates.description: Plan functional, evaluation, and acceptance testing.
activityTemplates.why: Validation runs smoothly only if it's planned in Build.
activityTemplates.consequence: Validation start is delayed.

activityTemplates.name: Document known limitations
activityTemplates.description: Record known failure modes and situations where the AI should not be used.
activityTemplates.why: Honest limitations protect users and set expectations.
activityTemplates.consequence: Users over-trust the AI.

activityTemplates.name: Prepare data and knowledge sources
activityTemplates.description: Clean, index, and govern the data or knowledge the AI depends on.
activityTemplates.why: Retrieval and grounding quality drive answer quality.
activityTemplates.consequence: Poor answers traced to stale or missing content.

activityTemplates.name: Implement guardrails and fallback behavior
activityTemplates.description: Add input/output filtering, confidence thresholds, and graceful fallbacks.
activityTemplates.why: Guardrails contain the impact when the AI is wrong.
activityTemplates.consequence: Unsafe or off-policy outputs reach users.

activityTemplates.name: Implement human review and override controls
activityTemplates.description: Build the review queue, override, and kill-switch controls.
activityTemplates.why: High-risk AI requires working human controls, not just a design.
activityTemplates.consequence: Oversight design exists only on paper.

activityTemplates.name: Integrate with target systems
activityTemplates.description: Connect to CRM, ticketing, or other systems of record.
activityTemplates.why: Value comes from being in the workflow.
activityTemplates.consequence: Swivel-chair usage reduces adoption.

activityTemplates.name: Run evaluation and document results
activityTemplates.description: Execute the evaluation plan and document results against thresholds.
activityTemplates.why: This is the core evidence that the AI performs well enough.
activityTemplates.consequence: No defensible basis for deployment.

activityTemplates.name: Validate human oversight in practice
activityTemplates.description: Demonstrate that users can review, correct, and override AI output in the real workflow.
activityTemplates.why: Oversight that works on paper often fails under real workload.
activityTemplates.consequence: Blocks the Validate gate for moderate and high risk.

activityTemplates.name: Complete UAT
activityTemplates.description: Business users test the solution in realistic scenarios and sign off.
activityTemplates.why: The business must accept the solution before it touches real work.
activityTemplates.consequence: Deployment without business acceptance.

activityTemplates.name: Conduct risk review
activityTemplates.description: Review the risk register, mitigations, and open issues before production.
activityTemplates.why: Confirms mitigations are real and nothing material is unaddressed.
activityTemplates.consequence: Unreviewed risk goes to production.

activityTemplates.name: Complete security review
activityTemplates.description: Security assessment including prompt-injection and data leakage testing.
activityTemplates.why: AI introduces new attack surfaces that need explicit testing.
activityTemplates.consequence: Exploitable weaknesses in production.

activityTemplates.name: Complete privacy review
activityTemplates.description: Privacy impact review of personal data use, retention, and access.
activityTemplates.why: Personal data use must be lawful and proportionate.
activityTemplates.consequence: Regulatory and reputational exposure.

activityTemplates.name: Assess residual risk
activityTemplates.description: Document remaining risk after mitigation and recommend acceptance or further action.
activityTemplates.why: Leaders need to knowingly accept the risk that remains.
activityTemplates.consequence: Risk is accepted implicitly rather than explicitly.

activityTemplates.name: Obtain executive residual-risk acceptance
activityTemplates.description: Executive sponsor explicitly accepts the residual risk in writing.
activityTemplates.why: High-risk AI requires accountable, named risk acceptance.
activityTemplates.consequence: Blocks deployment of high-risk solutions.

activityTemplates.name: Run adversarial and bias testing
activityTemplates.description: Execute the adversarial test plan and remediate findings.
activityTemplates.why: High-risk AI must be stress-tested for misuse and unfair outcomes.
activityTemplates.consequence: Unknown failure modes in production.

activityTemplates.name: Complete production readiness checklist
activityTemplates.description: Confirm operational, security, and support readiness items.
activityTemplates.why: A structured checklist catches the boring things that cause outages.
activityTemplates.consequence: Avoidable go-live incidents.

activityTemplates.name: Define production monitoring plan
activityTemplates.description: Decide what to monitor in production, alert thresholds, and who responds.
activityTemplates.why: AI quality drifts. You need to know before your customers do.
activityTemplates.consequence: Blocks the Validate gate for moderate and high risk.

activityTemplates.name: Performance and load testing
activityTemplates.description: Test latency and throughput at expected production volume.
activityTemplates.why: Slow AI is abandoned AI.
activityTemplates.consequence: Poor user experience at scale.

activityTemplates.name: Obtain go-live approval
activityTemplates.description: Record the decision to release to production, with any conditions.
activityTemplates.why: Go-live is a business decision that must be explicit and owned.
activityTemplates.consequence: Release without accountable approval.

activityTemplates.name: Obtain governance board deployment approval
activityTemplates.description: Present evidence to the AI governance board for explicit approval.
activityTemplates.why: High-risk AI requires an independent approval beyond the sponsor.
activityTemplates.consequence: Blocks high-risk deployment.

activityTemplates.name: Stand up support model and runbook
activityTemplates.description: Define support tiers, escalation paths, and known-issue handling.
activityTemplates.why: Users need help on day one.
activityTemplates.consequence: Issues go unresolved and trust erodes.

activityTemplates.name: Deliver training and communications
activityTemplates.description: Train users, including when not to trust the AI, and communicate the rollout.
activityTemplates.why: Users must know how to use the AI and how to challenge it.
activityTemplates.consequence: Low adoption or over-reliance.

activityTemplates.name: Activate production monitoring and alerting
activityTemplates.description: Turn on the monitoring defined in the plan, with alerting to named owners.
activityTemplates.why: Monitoring must be live before users are.
activityTemplates.consequence: Silent failure in production.

activityTemplates.name: Confirm rollback plan
activityTemplates.description: Verify the AI can be disabled or rolled back safely and quickly.
activityTemplates.why: The ability to turn it off is a core control.
activityTemplates.consequence: Incidents can't be contained.

activityTemplates.name: Evaluate pilot at production scale
activityTemplates.description: Measure accuracy, overrides, and escalations on real production traffic during the pilot before full rollout.
activityTemplates.why: Offline evaluation never fully predicts production behavior; the pilot is where real-world performance is proven.
activityTemplates.consequence: Full rollout proceeds on lab results alone.

activityTemplates.name: Execute phased rollout
activityTemplates.description: Release to a pilot cohort first, then expand on evidence.
activityTemplates.why: Phased rollout limits blast radius.
activityTemplates.consequence: Full-scale exposure to undiscovered issues.

activityTemplates.name: Monitor performance and drift
activityTemplates.description: Review production quality, drift, and alert history on a set cadence.
activityTemplates.why: Production behavior diverges from test behavior over time.
activityTemplates.consequence: Gradual quality decay goes unnoticed.

activityTemplates.name: Operate incident management
activityTemplates.description: Detect, triage, and resolve AI incidents with a documented process.
activityTemplates.why: AI incidents need fast, consistent handling.
activityTemplates.consequence: Incidents escalate unnecessarily.

activityTemplates.name: Run periodic evaluation
activityTemplates.description: Re-run the evaluation suite on a schedule and after any change.
activityTemplates.why: Confirms the AI still meets the bar it was approved against.
activityTemplates.consequence: Approval basis silently expires.

activityTemplates.name: Measure adoption
activityTemplates.description: Track eligible vs. active users, frequency, and satisfaction.
activityTemplates.why: Unused AI delivers no value.
activityTemplates.consequence: Adoption problems are discovered too late.

activityTemplates.name: Measure realized value
activityTemplates.description: Compare realized value against the value hypothesis.
activityTemplates.why: Proves the investment and informs what to do next.
activityTemplates.consequence: Funding decisions are made without evidence.

activityTemplates.name: Collect user feedback
activityTemplates.description: Gather qualitative feedback and feature requests from users.
activityTemplates.why: Feedback drives the improvement backlog.
activityTemplates.consequence: Improvements target the wrong things.

activityTemplates.name: Conduct post-implementation review
activityTemplates.description: Capture lessons learned and compare outcomes to the original case.
activityTemplates.why: Builds organizational learning across the AI portfolio.
activityTemplates.consequence: Same mistakes repeat on the next initiative.

activityTemplates.name: Prioritize improvement backlog
activityTemplates.description: Prioritize improvements based on value, feedback, and incidents.
activityTemplates.why: Keeps investment pointed at the highest value.
activityTemplates.consequence: Improvement effort is unfocused.

activityTemplates.name: Re-assess risk after material changes
activityTemplates.description: Re-run risk assessment after model, data, or scope changes.
activityTemplates.why: Material changes can change the risk tier.
activityTemplates.consequence: Operating outside the approved risk envelope.

activityTemplates.name: Define retirement criteria
activityTemplates.description: Agree the conditions under which the solution should be retired.
activityTemplates.why: Responsible AI includes knowing when to stop.
activityTemplates.consequence: Zombie AI keeps running after it stops adding value.

gates.name: Opportunity Gate
gates.description: Confirms the opportunity is framed well enough to invest in assessment.

criteria.label: Problem statement documented
criteria.description: At least a sentence describing the problem in today's workflow.

criteria.label: Target users defined
criteria.description: Who uses or is affected by the solution.

criteria.label: Business outcome defined
criteria.description: A measurable outcome, not a feature.

criteria.label: Executive sponsor and product owner assigned

gates.name: Feasibility & Risk Gate
gates.description: Confirms the solution is feasible, the data is usable, risk is understood, and value is plausible.

criteria.label: Key stakeholders identified
criteria.description: Business owner, data owner, and security are named on the team.

gates.name: Design Gate
gates.description: Confirms there is an agreed design, an evaluation approach, human oversight, and success measures.

criteria.label: Success metrics defined with baselines and targets
criteria.description: At least two metrics with a baseline and a target.

gates.name: Build Gate
gates.description: Confirms a working, versioned solution exists with a test plan and documented limitations.

gates.name: Validation Gate
gates.description: Confirms the evidence supports putting the solution in front of real users.

criteria.label: No unmitigated high or critical risks
criteria.description: Every open high or critical risk has a mitigation and an owner.

gates.name: Go-Live Gate
gates.description: Confirms people, process, and monitoring are ready and go-live is explicitly approved.

gates.name: Operational Review Gate
gates.description: Confirms the solution is monitored, evaluated, adopted, and delivering measured value before entering improvement or retirement planning.

criteria.label: Value and adoption measured
criteria.description: At least two metrics with current values recorded.
